title: Componentwise coefficient cochain currying
statement: Let J be a site with object universe u+1 and morphism universe u and coefficient sheaf R and module sheaves in universe u+1. Assume sheafification and WEqualsLocallyBijective for additive sheaves. For unbounded cochain complexes P,Q,I of R-modules, let Tot(P,Q) be the signed direct-sum total sheaf tensor [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] and Hom(Q,I) the fixed product Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex]. Every chain map f:Tot(P,Q)→I has a unique chain map g:P→Hom(Q,I) such that for every integers a,b, site object U and local sections x,y, f^(a+b)(x tensor y) equals the (a,b,a+b) product projection of g^a(x), evaluated at y on the identity object over U. Pure tensors are taken before sheafification via coefficientTensorGenerator; no global generation assertion about sheaf tensor sections is made.

proof.text: Assemble the normalized degreewise Hom-tensor maps into an isomorphism Hom(P,Hom(Q,I)) ≅ Hom(Tot(P,Q),I). Invertibility is degreewise and the signed differential compatibility makes it a chain isomorphism.

Identify global sections of each Hom-complex term with ordinary cochains, using its product projections. The identification commutes with the Hom differential. View f as a closed degree-zero cochain, take its corresponding global section, and pull it back through the chain isomorphism. It remains closed, hence determines the chain map g.

The degreewise map defining equation and the component formula for the global-cochain identification give the asserted pure-tensor equality. For uniqueness, equality on identity evaluations determines each local Hom morphism by the presheaf tensor-Hom adjunction, and equality of all product projections determines every g^a.
